name: Corpay
description: Corpay sells business payment products rather than consumer ones: fuel cards and fleet management for trucking and vehicle fleets (plus electronic tolls and parking, mainly in Brazil), accounts-payable automation and cross-border foreign-exchange payments for companies, and corporate card programmes for hotel and travel spend. Revenue is mostly a percentage of the dollars its customers spend, plus fees and interest, with fuel a smaller part of growth as Corporate Payments (cross-border B2B) expands quickly. It buys back stock heavily, funded by about $10 billion of debt, and has never paid a dividend. It completed the acquisition of UK-listed foreign-exchange firm Alpha Group on 2025-10-31.

employees.note: About 11,800 associates in 34 countries, about 4,300 in the US.

businessLines.name: Vehicle Payments
businessLines.how: Fuel, toll and parking customers (fleets) pay a fee per transaction and a share of the fuel price spread, plus card and late fees; revenue follows transaction volume, fuel prices and the spread between what merchants are paid and customers are charged.

businessLines.name: Corporate Payments
businessLines.how: Fee or foreign-exchange margin on the payment volume businesses push through its accounts-payable automation, virtual cards and cross-border (B2B currency) payment services; revenue per dollar of spend is lower on large cross-border enterprise clients but volume is growing fast.

businessLines.name: Lodging Payments
businessLines.how: Charges hotels and travel suppliers a fee on room-night bookings made for workforce and travel customers (including emergency housing); falls when emergency or workforce travel volume falls.

businessLines.name: Other (gift cards and payroll cards)
businessLines.how: Fees to retailers for running gift-card programmes and per-transaction fees on payroll cards; revenue per transaction and volume driven.

brands.name: Corpay (fuel, tolls, parking, lodging, B2B payments)
brands.note: Operating brand; Vehicle Payments 47.2 percent of FY2025 revenue

brands.name: Alpha Group International plc
brands.note: UK B2B cross-border foreign-exchange provider, acquired 2025-10-31

brands.name: Mastercard minority interest
brands.note: Mastercard holds an interest in a Corpay entity with a limited six-month put right (and Corpay call right); the 10-K also notes a TPG limited partnership requiring minimum return payments of up to 1.6 times invested capital on a sale
